findings.evidence: `rg` hits: `PermutationExtension.lean:29` is the only new public theorem; raw `Equiv.Perm.exists_extending_pair` remains at `ExchangeableAtMonotone.lean:46` and `FullyExchangeable.lean:62`; Mathlib provides only the fully generic theorem at `Mathlib/Logic/Equiv/Fintype.lean:158`.
findings.fix: Add public finite wrappers, at least the more general `exists_perm_extending_castLE {m n} (hmn : m ≤ n) (k : Fin m → Fin n) (hk : Function.Injective k) : ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), ∀ i, σ (Fin.castLE hmn i) = k i`, then derive the strict-monotone roadmap form from `hk.injective` and use the wrappers at both call sites.
findings.issue: `PermutationExtension` only exposes `exists_strictMono_nat_extending_fin`; the natural finite API is still missing, while `ExchangeableAtMonotone.lean:46` and `FullyExchangeable.lean:62` instantiate `Equiv.Perm.exists_extending_pair` directly for the same extension problem.

summary: The new module is under-generalized for the roadmap-level permutation-extension API: it only publishes the Nat monotone self-map extension while the finite permutation extensions remain raw Mathlib instantiations at the call sites.
